transcript.text: Beko vented dryer, drum goes round fine but it's just blowing cold air. Had it about 6 years. What part do I need?

On a Beko vented dryer that tumbles but gives no heat, the fault is almost always in the **heating circuit**. Most of these parts sit together at the back of the machine.

## Most likely culprits (in order)

1. **Thermal cut-out (TCO) / overheat thermostat.** This is the most common cause. It's a safety device that trips if the dryer overheats, usually because of a blocked vent hose or fluff build-up. Some are one-shot and need replacing. Others have a small reset button.
2. **Heating element.** After about 6 years the coil can burn through. On many Beko models the element is sold as an assembly with the thermostats already fitted, so you replace it all in one go.
3. **Control thermostat.** This is less common, but it can fail open and stop the element getting power.

## Before buying anything

- **Check the venting first.** Look for a kinked, crushed or fluff-packed vent hose, a blocked wall vent, or lint packed around the filter housing. If the TCO tripped, this is probably why, and a new part will just trip again.
- **Unplug the dryer**, remove the back panel, and test each part with a multimeter on continuity or resistance:
  - TCO and thermostats should show continuity (near 0 Ω). Open circuit means it's faulty.
  - The element should read roughly **20–30 Ω** per coil. Open circuit (OL) means it has burnt out.
  - Look for a visible break in the coil too.

## Getting the right part

Find the **model number** on the sticker inside the door rim (e.g. DRVS62W, DV7110, DCR93161W). Search "[model number] heater element" or "thermal cut-out" on sites like eSpares, Partmaster or 4ourhouse. Beko parts vary between models, so don't buy by "looks the same."

**Most likely fix:** if the venting has been poor, it's the TCO, which costs about £10–15. If the venting is fine, it's more likely the element assembly at about £25–45. Test before you buy if you can.

If you post the model number, I can help narrow down the exact part.

It says DV7110 on the front but I can't get to the label at the back, it's wedged in an alcove. No multimeter either. The hose was blocked with fluff though, I've cleaned it out and it's still cold after 20 mins. Which part should I order?

**Order the thermostat / thermal cut-out kit first.** A blocked hose is the classic cause of the TCO tripping. Cleaning the hose won't bring the heat back, because the cut-out either needs resetting or replacing.

## Check this before ordering

- **Look for a reset button.** Some Beko thermostats have a small red or black button you press in. You'll still need the back panel off to reach it, so it's only worth checking if you're pulling the machine out anyway.
- **Find the model label in the door.** On most Beko dryers it's on a sticker **inside the door opening** (round the rim or on the door itself), not on the back. It should show the full model number and often a serial or product code. That helps make sure you get the right variant.

## What to order

Search **"Beko DV7110 thermostat kit"** or **"DV7110 thermal cut out."** These kits usually include both the TCO and the control thermostat and cost about **£10–20**.

## If that doesn't fix it

The next suspect is the **heating element**. Search **"Beko DV7110 heater element."** It may come with the thermostats fitted, at roughly **£25–45**. Running hot against a blocked vent can also burn out the element. If you'd rather do one order and one repair, buying the element assembly could cover both. Just check the listing says it includes the thermostats.

## Fitting tips

- **Unplug it first**, then remove the back panel. The element and thermostats are at the back, so you'll have to pull it out of the alcove for the repair regardless.
- Take a photo of the wiring before you disconnect anything.
- While the back is off, hoover out any fluff around the element housing. That's a fire risk and may have contributed to the trip.

A cheap multimeter (about £10) would let you test the old parts and confirm which one failed, but it isn't essential if you just go part by part.
